Subject: Initial ask — POC sizing and hold window

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move the POC into our prod-like run (3-week window) starting ~Aug 3. Before we lock timelines internally, two asks:

1) Can you confirm node-level availability (A100-class) for an allocation of ~8 concurrent slots (8 x 80GB equivalent) across the US-west region for the Aug 3–24 window?
2) Can Redwood provide a provisional soft-hold for that window while we finalize procurement paperwork? We need the soft-hold to be non-billable and to carry an expiry (we will confirm by July 27).

Attached is a short requirements PDF with task mix and expected concurrency. Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Tom

Subject: Re: Initial ask — POC sizing and hold window

Markus / team —

Quick availability summary after a short inventory sweep and scheduler projection:

- US-west pool (g4/g5-equivalent A100-class): baseline free capacity today can support 6 concurrent 80GB-equivalent slots without disrupting reserved capacity for existing customers.
- We can reach 8 concurrent slots during Aug 3–24 if we activate two short-term measures:
  * Apply a provisional soft-hold on 12 warm nodes (node tags: LUM-POC-CLAIM-01..12) which allows us to pre-reserve packing slots while keeping nodes available for emergency preemption.
  * Enable temporary tighter packing (reduce per-request headroom) via a one-time tiling override for the POC window. Ops will monitor to ensure latency SLOs are not violated.

Constraints & notes:
- Thermal affinity: a subset of our US-west racks (rack-west-3) have maintenance planned Aug 10—12. We recommend avoiding full placement in rack-west-3 to reduce disruption risk.
- Soft-hold expiry: we can set an internal soft-hold that expires 2025-07-27 23:59 UTC. After expiry the slots will revert to general availability unless the hold is promoted to a committed reservation.
- Non-billable: soft-hold will be non-billable, but converting to committed reserved capacity will require the standard Dedicated contract.

Action items (ops):
1) I will open OPS-4521 and attach a provisional slot mapping.
2) Soojin — can you run a quick packing simulation with the attached gpu-slot-matrix.csv and confirm the exact node IDs we should tag?
3) Laura / Markus — confirm whether Luminary needs cross-region failover (we can add standby nodes in US-east for an incremental cost).

Attachments included: redwood_provisional-hold-template.xlsx, gpu-slot-matrix.csv

Ben Carter
Capacity & Provisioning Lead — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Initial ask — POC sizing and hold window

Ben / Markus / Tom —

I ran the packing simulation against the current slot matrix and validated node candidates. Summary:

- Candidate nodes (node-id shorthand): nw-usw-12a, nw-usw-12b, nw-usw-14c, nw-usw-16a, nw-usw-16b, nw-usw-18a, nw-usw-20a, nw-usw-21b, nw-usw-22a, nw-usw-22b, nw-usw-24c, nw-usw-25a
- Recommended placement: avoid >2 nodes in rack-west-3 during Aug 10–12 maintenance window. Use nw-usw-16*/18*/20*/21* as primary.
- Soft-hold mechanics: I will tag the nodes with tags: LUM-POC-CLAIM-01..12 and create a time-limited hold using OPS-4521. The hold will have metadata: expiry=2025-07-27T23:59:00Z, hold_type=provisional_nonbillable, owner=markus_klein.
- Fallbacks: if capacity dips during the window we will automatically route to a quantized 4-bit variant (model-level fallback) for non-critical workloads to preserve throughput. That fallback requires Luminary sign-off — Tom, is that acceptable for background batch jobs?

Next steps:
- I will create OPS-4521 with the tags and a draft runbook for activation. Expect a follow-up once OPS ticket is created (~30–60 minutes).
- Markus / Laura: please confirm HubSpot deal id to link the hold to the commercial record.

Soojin Lee
